content: He who would truly fight for justice, if he would survive even for a short time, must lead a private rather than a public life.
author: Socrates
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Socrates understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
